claims.text: Combining advanced free-energy sampling, phase-field modeling, and tailored thermal processing will enable precise control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
The proposed method will quantitatively map the free-energy landscape governing diffusion-controlled transformations.
As-cast or solution-treated Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs have multiphase or complex-phase microstructures.
Monte Carlo or molecular-dynamics-based sampling can provide the free-energy maps needed for this approach.
Phase-field simulations can be combined with free-energy maps to design suitable annealing temperatures, cooling rates, and dwell times.
High-temperature processing under an inert atmosphere and controlled annealing and cooling will permit sufficient atomic diffusion.
The free-energy landscape and diffusion kinetics mediate the sequence and stability of phase transformations in the HEA.
Mapping the free-energy landscape reveals optimal thermal parameters for driving or suppressing diffusion-controlled phase separation.
Annealing temperature can alter phase decomposition and phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni-related HEAs.
Thermal profiles derived from the maps will steer thermodynamic and kinetic pathways toward a desired microstructure.
The proposed approach will overcome limitations of empirical thermal treatments.
The approach will produce more predictable and tunable phase evolution with controlled phase fractions.
The resulting material properties will be enhanced relative to those obtained by conventional thermal processing.
Generic heat treatments and cooling rates yield less controlled phase evolution in multiphase HEAs.
The effectiveness of the method may be limited by free-energy sampling accuracy, extreme diffusion regimes, and inability to reproduce predicted thermal profiles.
Local compositional variations may introduce uncertainty into phase-evolution predictions.
The magnitude and reproducibility of the proposed improvement remain unquantified in complex multicomponent systems.
